$comment: Authoritative simulation constants. Values are decimal; the loader converts them to Q16.16 once at startup and the simulation never sees a float again. Editing this file is the supported way to rebalance — no constant that affects gameplay is allowed to live in a .ts or .wgsl source.

world.$comment: The w extent is deliberately narrower than x/y/z. A 4D world with equal extents in all four axes puts almost every entity far off the viewing hyperplane at any moment, and reads as an empty room. Compressing w keeps the population near the slice the player occupies.

tick.$comment: maxCatchUpTicks bounds the accumulator so a stalled tab cannot queue thousands of ticks and freeze on resume — the spiral-of-death guard. Time past the bound is discarded, not simulated.

physics.$comment: Gravity acts only along y. A 4D world has no privileged 'down' — the choice is a design decision that gives the player a stable frame of reference, not a physical necessity. restitution below 1 guarantees bounce energy strictly decreases, which is what keeps the boundary response from pumping energy into the system.

rendering.$comment: mode is 'project' (4D perspective divide along w) or 'slice' (3D cross-section at the viewer's w). Projection shows the whole object distorted; slicing shows a true cross-section that changes shape as objects move through w.

gpu.$comment: 64 lanes is the common denominator that maps cleanly onto AMD wave64, NVIDIA warp32 (two per group) and Apple SIMD32. Raising it risks occupancy loss on tile GPUs; the WGSL @workgroup_size attribute must be edited to match, as WGSL requires a compile-time literal.
